locator: ch. 3, para. 1: propter auctoritatem [i]psius Dei revelantis, qui nec falli nec fallere potest
interpretation: The council defines faith as believing revealed things true not for their intrinsic truth seen by natural reason but for the authority of God revealing, 'qui nec falli nec fallere potest'. Read as a commitment about God as revealer: he can neither be deceived nor deceive. The relative clause is asserted, not argued; its defense belongs to the divine attributes (stage 2). The text does not say that a body God founded is likewise protected from error; that is the further content of the bridge premise it bears on. Witness: vatican.va Latin page (ASS 5), whose OCR-style typos ('psius' for 'ipsius') are read as noise.
